title: Bid path stays pure
what_happened: Bid requests go HTTP parse, in-memory match, bid or no-bid, async log. No LLM or database on that path.
impact: Decision time averages about 41 microseconds.
lesson_or_next_step: Never add an LLM, Postgres, ClickHouse, S3 or a compile step to the bid path.

title: Money is integer micros
what_happened: Caps and spend are stored as integer micros. Billable impressions include qty.multiplier once.
impact: No float rounding errors on money.
lesson_or_next_step: Every new money field uses micros. Tests must cover the multiplier.

title: SSPs plug in behind an adapter
what_happened: SSP_ADAPTER=simulator by default. The VIOOH adapter is a stub.
impact: A live exchange can be added without touching matching.
lesson_or_next_step: Write each new SSP as an adapter, never as changes to the matcher.

title: Product agents run on Grok, off the bid path
what_happened: Runtime agents in agents/ call the xAI API. They audit and plan, never bid.
impact: Keeps AI cost and latency away from bidding.
lesson_or_next_step: Revisit the model choice when the Central Brain is designed (Sprint 4).

title: Claude plans, Cursor builds, Claude Code reviews
what_happened: Sam chose one owner per job: Claude chat writes specs and tasks, Cursor builds one task per branch, Claude Code reviews before merge. Grok is out of the build loop.
impact: Three AI tools stop drifting apart.
lesson_or_next_step: Handoff is always a task file in tasks/. No verbal-only instructions.

title: Dashboard KPIs cover the full campaign window
what_happened: GB/IE split came from the last 500 events while totals came from the hourly view.
impact: Two numbers on one screen described different periods.
lesson_or_next_step: Totals and splits must come from the same query window. No silent row caps.

title: dooh-dsp is the main build
what_happened: The earlier Adstreet repo and its Cloudflare plan are retired.
impact: One codebase to grow into the company.
lesson_or_next_step: Ignore Adstreet docs when planning.

title: Ireland first
what_happened: Launch in Dublin, then the rest of Ireland, Northern Ireland, then the UK.
impact: Irish rules (Alcohol Act, ASAI) come first in the compliance engine.
lesson_or_next_step: Design compliance per country so the UK can be added later.

title: Own DSP, bootstrapped, go-live in about four months
what_happened: Connect to SSPs directly with no reseller DSP. Prototype in 2-3 months, then UAT, go-live around March 2027.
impact: Control over bidding is the moat. No outside money for now.
lesson_or_next_step: Keep running costs low. Prefer free tiers and test modes until UAT.

title: EUR is the base currency
what_happened: Each advertiser and campaign carries a currency, default EUR. GBP stays possible for NI and UK.
impact: Avoids a rewrite when expanding to the UK.
lesson_or_next_step: Never hard-code a currency symbol. Format with the currency code.

title: Three parallel lanes, one planner, one reviewer
what_happened: Cursor builders in Trading, Platform and Experience lanes (Agents from Sprint 3). Each owns its folders and works from task files.
impact: Faster than one agent without agents colliding on shared files.
lesson_or_next_step: More than three or four at once overloads review. Contracts make parallel work safe.

title: Prototype launch scope
what_happened: Businesses and creators first. No alcohol, gambling or political ads in the prototype.
impact: Removes the highest legal and reputational risks from the first release.
lesson_or_next_step: Compliance gate must hard-block these categories until a decision lifts it.

title: Priority order follows the go-live critical path
what_happened: Sam asked to build what is most core and urgent first. Every item gets P0/P1/P2. Within P0, anything an SSP checks during certification goes first.
impact: If time runs short, what is missing is polish, not a go-live item.
lesson_or_next_step: A free lane always takes the highest item in tasks/BACKLOG.md for its lane.

title: Rename of brain to compiler parked
what_happened: The rename touched every lane and paused all builders for no customer or SSP benefit. Removed from task 005.
impact: Saves a full cross-lane freeze in Sprint 0.
lesson_or_next_step: Do cosmetic cross-lane changes only after go-live.

title: Cursor CLI on Sam's laptop as the build runtime
what_happened: Sam chose local Cursor CLI agents (option 1) over Cursor cloud agents.
impact: Commits stay under Sam's name and nothing runs on someone else's machine.
lesson_or_next_step: Laptop must be on, awake and running Claude while agents work.

title: Shared handbook for every new agent
what_happened: handbook/ explains mission, DOOH basics, architecture, Irish ad rules, roadmap and team in about ten minutes of reading.
impact: New agents get up to speed without re-reading the whole repo.
lesson_or_next_step: Keep the handbook short. Update it after each merge that changes how things work.

title: Contracts before cross-lane work
what_happened: contracts/events.md and contracts/advertiser-app.md fix the shapes lanes build against.
impact: Lanes can build in parallel and still fit together.
lesson_or_next_step: Builders never change a contract. They stop and ask.

title: Sole authorship on GitHub
what_happened: No Co-authored-by, Made-with or Generated-with lines. A commit-msg hook strips them and Claude Code attribution is off.
impact: Sam is the only author on the repo.
lesson_or_next_step: Run git config core.hooksPath .githooks once per clone. Check new branches for trailers.

title: Each Cursor agent works in its own git worktree
what_happened: The bridge creates a separate checkout per job in dooh-dsp-worktrees next to the repo.
impact: Agents never collide with each other or with Sam's own uncommitted changes.
lesson_or_next_step: Remove finished worktrees with cursor_remove_worktree once the branch is pushed.

title: Claude starts and watches Cursor agents from chat
what_happened: cursor-bridge desktop extension: start a task, check status, read output, stop, clean up. Max 3 at once, 90-minute timeout.
impact: No copy-pasting between Claude and Cursor.
lesson_or_next_step: Check GitHub branches for progress, since text output only arrives when a job ends.

title: Build log kept as one matrix
what_happened: Every decision, workflow, mistake, win, idea, risk and open question goes into docs/build-log.csv. Builders add Log entries in their Builder report and the planner copies them in after merge.
impact: Agents can filter past lessons by area before starting a task.
lesson_or_next_step: One writer (the planner) so parallel branches never conflict on the log.

title: Copy failed on a __pycache__ folder and the commit was skipped
what_happened: Copying the bridge folder hit a cache directory and stopped the script before commit.
impact: Lost a round trip; nothing broken.
lesson_or_next_step: Copy files explicitly and never commit cache folders.

title: GitHub CLI token in Claude's workspace is invalid
what_happened: Could not open pull requests from the cloud workspace.
impact: Sam had to open the setup PR himself from a link.
lesson_or_next_step: Check gh auth before promising a PR. Agents on Sam's PC push branches; PRs opened from there or by Sam.

title: Connector config written where the Store version of Claude doesn't read
what_happened: The Microsoft Store app reads its config from a LocalCache folder, not APPDATA.
impact: First setup run showed no connector.
lesson_or_next_step: Check which install (Store or direct) before writing app config.

title: Local servers in claude_desktop_config.json don't reach cloud chat sessions
what_happened: After two setup runs the connector still didn't appear in chat. Only desktop extensions (.mcpb) are exposed there.
impact: About an hour lost on the wrong install method.
lesson_or_next_step: For tools Claude chat must use, ship a desktop extension, not a config entry.

title: Python couldn't start the Cursor CLI on Windows (WinError 193)
what_happened: The Cursor CLI on Windows is a PowerShell/cmd script, not an exe.
impact: Jobs would have failed to start.
lesson_or_next_step: Launch .ps1 through powershell.exe and .cmd through cmd.exe.

title: Setup read 'Not logged in' as logged in
what_happened: The check matched the words 'logged in' inside 'Not logged in', so the login step was skipped.
impact: Sam was never asked to log in.
lesson_or_next_step: Always test status parsing against the negative message too.

title: Extension saved with the repo's tools subfolder, and the fix didn't apply
what_happened: Sam picked dooh-dsp/tools. Changing the setting didn't reach the running extension until a reinstall.
impact: Two extra round trips with Sam before agents could start.
lesson_or_next_step: Tolerate near-miss input: the bridge now walks up to the repo root (v0.2.1).

title: Job status race in the bridge
what_happened: The server rewrote the job file after starting the runner and could wipe the agent PID, which would break stop.
impact: Caught in local testing before it reached Sam's PC.
lesson_or_next_step: One writer per file: the runner owns its job record.

title: Bridge tested against a fake Cursor agent first
what_happened: Ran start, status, stop and cleanup on a throwaway repo before installing anything on Sam's PC.
impact: Caught the status race and the stop bug early.
lesson_or_next_step: Test tooling locally with a stand-in before using real accounts.

title: Three Cursor agents started in parallel from chat
what_happened: Tasks 002, 003 and 004 started at 19:06. Each pushed its first commit within about two minutes, under Sam's name, with no attribution lines.
impact: First fully hands-off build loop.
lesson_or_next_step: Keep task files self-contained so agents can start without questions.

title: Jobs work with or without a separate Node install
what_happened: If only Claude's built-in Node exists, the extension supervises jobs itself instead of a separate runner.
impact: No extra install needed on Sam's PC.
lesson_or_next_step: Design desktop tools to fall back gracefully.

title: Show Cursor progress live
what_happened: Switch the bridge to Cursor's streaming output so the log shows each step while a job runs.
impact: Sam and Claude can see progress without waiting for the end.
lesson_or_next_step: Do it in the next bridge update.

title: Use Cursor cloud agents
what_happened: Run builders in Cursor's cloud instead of on the laptop.
impact: Laptop would not need to stay on.
lesson_or_next_step: Rejected for now: their commits show 'Cursor Agent' as author, which breaks sole authorship.

title: Customers prepare an ad like an Instagram post
what_happened: Self-serve creative flow with OOH rules and each SSP's rules checked as they build it.
impact: Core of the 'anyone can advertise' promise.
lesson_or_next_step: Compliance engine (Sprint 3) and creative studio (Sprint 4).

title: Explain bidding inside the app
what_happened: Show customers how CPM, screen plays and auctions decide what they pay.
impact: Builds trust with first-time advertisers.
lesson_or_next_step: Part of the Advertiser App plan and estimate screens.

title: Every customer gets their own AI agent
what_happened: Each advertiser's agent runs their campaign and talks to the company's agents and a central brain.
impact: AI-native service at SME prices.
lesson_or_next_step: Advertiser Agent v1 and Central Brain v1 in Sprint 4.

title: Ops system with chat to company agents
what_happened: Employees work through a chat interface to the right agents, under a central brain that knows all workflows.
impact: Small team can run an enterprise-scale operation.
lesson_or_next_step: Ops Console chat after accounts and roles exist.

title: Launch date is set by SSP certification, not by code
what_happened: No SSP agreement yet. Certification needs an integration spec, a sandbox and test time.
impact: Code can be ready and still not go live.
lesson_or_next_step: Sam to start outreach to VIOOH, JCDecaux and other SSPs now.

title: Repo is public
what_happened: Bidding logic and the compliance rulebook are visible to anyone.
impact: Competitors can copy the approach.
lesson_or_next_step: Make the repo private and move it to a company GitHub organisation.

title: No staging cloud account yet
what_happened: Staging is needed from Sprint 1 for accounts, payments and pilot testing.
impact: Sprint 1 slips without it.
lesson_or_next_step: Sam to choose a provider and create the account.

title: Is pull request #1 (perf/bidder-latency) Sam's?
what_happened: An older PR touches the bidder.
impact: Could conflict with task 003 or the p99 work.
lesson_or_next_step: Sam to confirm; merge, close or hand to the Trading lane.

title: Do Sam's uncommitted changes in agents/ matter?
what_happened: Sam's local clone has uncommitted edits in agents/.
impact: They are not on GitHub, so no agent can build on them.
lesson_or_next_step: Sam to commit, share or discard. Agents never touch them.

title: Claude reviews from chat, no need to open Claude Code
what_happened: Claude chat can run the reviewer and security checklists on a pushed branch directly, the same ones Claude Code uses.
impact: Sam only merges; review starts as soon as an agent finishes.
lesson_or_next_step: Review each task the moment it finishes; don't wait for all three.

title: Make recurring work AI native
what_happened: Sam wants recurring build work turned into reusable agents: Cursor commands for repeat task types and scheduled agents for routine checks.
impact: Repeat work becomes one command instead of a new brief each time.
lesson_or_next_step: Planner to propose the first set; Sam picks.

title: Sam signs off business logic before it is built
what_happened: Any task with rules about money, pricing, customers, approvals or compliance lists them in plain words and waits for Sam's approval. Agents build only backlog work.
impact: Agents build fast without inventing policy.
lesson_or_next_step: Planner writes Business rules in every task and gets sign-off before marking it ready.

title: Morning build report and nightly checks
what_happened: Two scheduled agents: a CEO-level build report every morning, and a nightly run of tests and security checks on main.
impact: Sam stays informed without asking; problems are caught overnight.
lesson_or_next_step: Report flags only what needs Sam; tech detail stays out.

title: Finished work sat unreviewed for up to 15 minutes
what_happened: All three agents finished between 19:20 and 19:27, but the next check was set for a fixed time (19:35), so nobody reviewed them until Sam asked.
impact: Wasted time and Sam's trust.
lesson_or_next_step: React when a job finishes, never on a timer alone. The hourly build watcher plus checks after every start cover it.

title: Cursor CLI text output comes back empty on Windows
what_happened: Every job's output.log held only the bridge's start and end lines, so Claude couldn't read the agents' final reports there.
impact: Had to read reports from the task files on GitHub instead.
lesson_or_next_step: Read the Builder report in the task file on the branch. Try stream-json output in the next bridge update.

title: Reviews caught real money bugs before merge
what_happened: Security and code review on 003 found that a crafted notice could book negative spend and that an unset signing key let anyone forge charges. 004's review found negative wallet top-ups and a framework version with a critical vulnerability.
impact: None of these reached main.
lesson_or_next_step: Keep security review on anything touching money.

title: First three tasks built in under 25 minutes each
what_happened: Cursor agents finished 002, 003 and 004 in 14, 21 and 19 minutes, and both fix rounds took under 10 minutes.
impact: Build speed is no longer the bottleneck; review and Sam's decisions are.
lesson_or_next_step: Keep task files tight and decisions ready ahead of the agents.

title: Revenue model: subscriptions plus campaign fee plus percentage
what_happened: Sam proposed monthly plans (basic, premium, complete) or a fee per campaign, plus a percentage that is lower for subscribers. Planner recommended: hold funds at launch, flat campaign fee kept at launch, percentage settled on what actually ran, unused budget refunded.
impact: Sets how the company makes money and its margins.
lesson_or_next_step: Waiting on Sam: fee on top or inside budget, first customer type, prices now or after pilots.

title: Brain CI fix split into its own task
what_happened: CI is red on an old brain memory bug. Wrote task 006 for the Trading lane instead of skipping the test.
impact: Green CI becomes a real signal again.
lesson_or_next_step: Never skip a failing test to get green; write the fix task.

title: Nightly check 2026-10-31
what_happened: Nightly check on main found the known brain test failure (task 006), a Next.js version with critical vulnerabilities in the Ops Console, and outdated Pillow, Starlette and python-multipart with known vulnerabilities in the Python services; no committed secrets were found.
impact: Nothing is deployed yet so exposure is local; these must be fixed before staging.
lesson_or_next_step: Planner to write upgrade tasks: apps/web next 15.5.28 or later; Python services pillow 13+, fastapi with starlette 1.3.1+, python-multipart 0.0.31+.
